customManagers.description: Keep Cloudflare Workers' compatibility_date moving. It is a hand-maintained date with no package behind it, so no manager covers it and it silently freezes at whatever a project was scaffolded with, leaving no way to tell a deliberate pin from a forgotten one. Versions come from workerd's release tags rather than today's date, so a proposed date can never be one the deployed runtime has not shipped. Raising it opts into runtime behaviour changes, so the automerge rule excludes this manager and the bump lands as a reviewable PR

packageRules.description: Automerge non-major updates only; major updates require manual review

mcr.microsoft.com and ghcr.io serve tag lists without release timestamps, and the default timestamp-required behaviour reads a missing timestamp as not-yet-aged -- so minimumReleaseAge holds those updates indefinitely rather than for its stated window, with nothing to show why. Docker Hub does return timestamps and keeps aging normally; add a registry here only after checking it serves none. Aging resumes on its own if one starts serving them
Group Playwright's npm packages with the container image that ships their browsers; the image bundles browsers built for one Playwright version, so a split update breaks E2E runs
